items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: And then later on, there was a girl named Harris. She moved to Everett and she came into high school.

ctx.x: Yeah, I remember his name. And then later on, there was a girl named Harris. She moved to Everett and she came into high school. But there was very few, and that's why I had a fight. Them Italians and the Jews and the Irishmen, they'd all gang. When the bell rang in school, I tried to get in the front lines, see. And they'd try to head me off, try to block me. But I usually got in that front line. And when I got out that door, I was gone. Because if I didn't, I'd have to fight.

And I'd fight and I'd beat the kid up, and he'd go home and tell his mother and his mother would come up to my mother and say, your son beat my son. I said, well, he called me a nigger. I beat him up.
